Refactor weapon fire rates as beat subdivisions and add catalogue-wide on-grid invariant

## Summary
Replace the hard-coded fire-rate constants in `src/utils/weapons.ts` with values derived from the 80 BPM beat period. Each weapon fires at an exact subdivision: cannon 2/beat (375 ms), spread 1/beat (750 ms), dual 1/beat (750 ms), rapid 6/beat (125 ms). Add a catalogue-wide test asserting every fire rate divides evenly into the beat period.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — All `WEAPON_*_FIRE_RATE` constants in `src/utils/weapons.ts` become derived from the beat period (e.g. `beatPeriodMs / subdivisions`), not hard-coded literals.
- [ ] **AC2** — `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` fire rates match the producer-specified values: cannon 375 ms (2/beat), spread 750 ms (1/beat), dual 750 ms (1/beat), rapid 125 ms (6/beat).
- [ ] **AC3** — A catalogue-wide invariant test asserts `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` for every weapon in `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`.
- [ ] **AC4** — Existing weapon tests still pass after the refactor (no behaviour change beyond timing).
- [ ] **AC5** — New weapons added to the catalogue must satisfy the invariant; the test fails if they do not.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC3** — [ ] **AC3 — Per-weapon subdivisions + catalogue-wide invariant.** Each weapon's fire interval is an exact subdivision of the beat: **cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat)**, **spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat)**. A catalogue-wide test asserts every `WeaponDefinition.fireRateMs` satisfies `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` (equivalently `fireRateMs × n === beatPeriodMs` for a positive integer `n`), so the future 20 BPM quarter-time weapon and any other new weapon are on-grid by construction.

## Key Files
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — fire rates derived from beat period.
- `src/utils/weapons.test.ts` — invariant test.

## Risks
- Low: existing tests will verify no unintended behaviour changes. The rapid weapon (125 ms) is unchanged; cannon, spread, and dual rates change slightly.
data.title: Refactor weapon fire rates as beat subdivisions and add catalogue-wide invariant

Replace Player.tryFire per-weapon cooldowns with phase-locked beat scheduling

## Summary
Replace the independent per-weapon cooldown model in `Player.tryFire` with phase-locked scheduling on the shared beat clock. A weapons next shot time is the smallest multiple of its interval at/after the current beat-clock time. Collection may delay the first shot to the next grid tick (by design). All active weapons share the same anchor so they stay phase-locked.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — `Player.tryFire(dt)` no longer uses independent per-weapon cooldowns — every shot is snapped to the shared beat clock.
- [ ] **AC2** — All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns).
- [ ] **AC3** — A weapon collected mid-beat fires its first shot on the next grid tick (by design).
- [ ] **AC4** — Cumulative and timed weapon semantics are unchanged (collection, expiry, reset all work as before).
- [ ] **AC5** — Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick, verified with multiple active weapons.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC2** — [ ] **AC2 — All player fire is globally quantised.** Player auto-fire (`Player.tryFire` and its callers in `CombatScene`/`GymWeapons`) emits shots only on ticks of the shared beat clock, phase-locked to the scene/beat anchor — never off-grid — regardless of when a weapon is collected or the frame rate. All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns). Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick.

## Key Files
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `tryFire` / cooldown model → phase-locked scheduling.
- `src/entities/Player.test.ts` — grid-tick emission tests.

## Risks
- Medium: this changes the core fire model. Must preserve cumulative/timed weapon semantics. Tests must verify phase-locking with multiple active weapons.
data.title: Replace Player.tryFire per-weapon cooldowns with phase-locked beat scheduling

# Wire the runtime auto-sequencer into the game's wave generation

## Problem statement

The runtime auto-sequencer (`src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`, AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X) is a standalone pure-core library — nothing in the playable game calls it. Enemy composition is still hard-coded in `src/waves/Formations.ts` (`LEVELS`) and driven through `WaveManager` by `PlayScene`, so every run uses the same fixed waves. This item wires the sequencer into a playable run so wave composition is generated at runtime from a target difficulty curve, behind an opt-in config toggle, with the static campaign preserved as the default and the fallback.

## Users

- As a **player**, when the feature is enabled, enemy waves should follow a difficulty curve so each run ramps up smoothly instead of using identical fixed enemy counts. (Default-off means shipped behaviour is unchanged until enabled.)
- As a **designer**, I want to define the campaign's levels, names, wave counts and per-wave difficulty targets in a CSV config, so I can tune the difficulty ramp and campaign shape without editing `Formations.ts`.

## Decisions confirmed at intake

1. **Opt-in toggle, default off.** Static `LEVELS` remains the shipped default; generated waves only drive the run when the toggle is enabled in config. A follow-on work item covers *mixing* generated and scripted levels within one campaign: **Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD)** (sibling, `discovered-from`).
2. **Per-level curves with configurable per-level wave counts.** One `sequencer()` call per level; the curve length sets the wave count.
3. **Fully data-driven campaign skeleton.** The curve config also defines the level count and level names (not just targets). The boss is still triggered after the final configured level (existing `WaveManager` behaviour).
4. **CSV-backed config.** A new `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` is loaded through the existing `configStore`/CSV pipeline (editable in dev via `/api/csv/...`, bundled read-only in production).
5. **Defaults seeded from current calibration.** The baked-in default targets are derived from the current `LEVELS` measured scores (`levelDifficulty`/`enemyDifficulty`) spread non-decreasingly across each level's waves.

## Existing state

- `WaveManager` already accepts injected `LevelDefinition[]` via its constructor and `setLevels()`, defaulting to static `LEVELS`; it owns plan/spawn/progression and the boss trigger.
- `sequencer(curve, candidates, options)` returns one `ShootableWave` per curve entry, each with one adjusted group and a `shootEnabled` flag; `options.defaultShootEnabled` applies to the whole call, which is why generation is done **per level** (so Levels 1–3 and 4–5 can differ).
- `AdjustedGroup` extends `WaveGroup`, so `ShootableWave.groups` maps structurally to `WaveDefinition.groups`.
- Config tunables live in two pipelines: CSV-backed `configStore`/`csv.ts`/Vite plugin (enemies, ship) and the localStorage-backed `rules.ts` (`GameRules`).
- GDD §2.4 — Levels 1–3 do not fire; §2.5 — Levels 4–5 do. §3.2 fixes level themes.

## Desired change

At run start, `PlayScene` reads the config. When the (opt-in) toggle is disabled it uses static `LEVELS` exactly as today. When enabled it builds a `LevelDefinition[]` from the difficulty-curve config by calling `sequencer()` once per configured level with `defaultShootEnabled = levelNumber >= 4`, converts each `ShootableWave` to a `WaveDefinition`, injects the result into `WaveManager`, and drives the run from it. Any empty/degenerate config falls back to static `LEVELS`.

## Constraints

- **Pure core stays pure.** `difficultySequencer.ts` is not modified (read-only call site).
- **Determinism.** Generation must be a pure function of config + candidate pool; no RNG.
- **No behavioural change when the toggle is off.** Existing `WaveManager`/`PlayScene`/campaign tests must pass unchanged.
- **CSV is the source of truth in dev**; production reads the bundled copy; malformed rows must not crash.
- Follow the existing config/CSV patterns (codec, plugin, store) rather than inventing a new persistence path.
- UK English in prose; Markdown in the work item.

## Assumptions

- The global opt-in toggle is a scalar tunable and will live in the existing `GameRules` settings store (`sequencedWavesEnabled`, default `false`); the per-level curve values/targets live in the CSV. Per-level source mixing is deferred to AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD.
- The campaign fire rule is derived from the (1-based) level number: `level <= 3` ⇒ `shootEnabled=false`, `level >= 4` ⇒ `true`. With a data-driven skeleton this applies to any configured levels beyond 5 as firing levels; per-level `shootEnabled` overrides are out of scope.
- "Configurable curve" is satisfied by the CSV-backed config plus the baked-in default; runtime UI editing is AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL.

## Acceptance criteria

- **WaveManager accepts injected definitions** — `WaveManager` is driven by generated `LevelDefinition`/`WaveDefinition` data; with no override supplied it uses static `LEVELS` exactly, and existing `WaveManager` tests pass unchanged.
- **Opt-in toggle** — with the toggle disabled (the default) the run uses static `LEVELS` and behaves as today; with it enabled the run uses generated definitions (test asserts both paths).
- **Runtime generation runs** — at run start, with the toggle enabled, the game builds per-level curves from the curve config and calls `sequencer()` once per level, obtaining a `SequencerResult` per level.
- **CSV-backed, data-driven config** — `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` defines level number, level name and per-wave targets (curve length ⇒ wave count); it is loaded through the existing CSV/configStore pipeline and is editable in dev / read-only in production. Malformed or missing rows fall back to the baked-in default curve without crashing.
- **Generated waves drive the run** — the groups produced by the sequencer are what `PlayScene` spawns (verified via the spawn plan / `WaveManager.planSpawns()` or a test harness), not the static `LEVELS`.
- **Curve is configurable** — changing the configured/default curve changes the produced wave composition; two distinct curves yield different plans (test asserts this).
- **Campaign fire rule** — generated levels 1–3 have `shootEnabled=false`; levels 4+ have `shootEnabled=true` (test asserts both).
- **Determinism** — generating the campaign twice with the same config and candidate pool yields identical level/wave definitions.
- **Fallback is safe** — an empty/degenerate curve config, an empty curve, or an empty candidate pool falls back to static `LEVELS` and the game does not crash (test covers the fallback).
- **Testing/validation** — new unit/integration tests cover the codec, campaign builder, conversion, fire rule, determinism and fallback, and they are meaningful and passing.
- **Documentation** — all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **No regressions** — the full project test suite passes with the new changes (`npm test`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — existing sequencer; read-only call site (`sequencer`, `defaultCandidatePool`, `ShootableWave`, `AdjustedGroup`).
- `src/core/csv.ts` — add a difficulty-curve codec (parse/serialize + validation, mirroring `EnemyConfig`).
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — add the difficulty-curve row/config types (leaf module, no imports).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — load `difficulty-curves.csv` through the existing dev/bundled pipeline and expose an accessor.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — add the opt-in `sequencedWavesEnabled` tunable (default `false`) to `GameRules`.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — **new** CSV defining levels, names, wave targets (data-driven skeleton).
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — **new**: build the curve config/pool and convert `SequencerResult` per level into `LevelDefinition[]` (plus fallback).
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — confirm/verify injected-definition support (minimal or no change).
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — static `LEVELS`: default/fallback and level metadata source for seeding defaults.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — build + inject the generated campaign at run start when the toggle is enabled.
- Vite CSV plugin / dev write endpoint — extend to serve the new CSV if the existing generic path does not already cover it.
- Test files: `src/core/csv.test.ts`, `src/core/configStore.test.ts`, `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` (**new**), `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **CSV pipeline scope** — extending the codec/plugin/store is the largest cost; mitigated by mirroring the existing `EnemyConfig` codec/plugin exactly and reusing the generic write endpoint where possible.
- **Default-curve calibration drift** — seeding from measured `LEVELS` scores could diverge from the static campaign if either changes; mitigated by a test asserting the default generated campaign is non-decreasing and stays in 0–100.
- **Fallback correctness** — a partial/degenerate CSV must never produce an unplayable campaign; mitigated by an explicit fallback test and a single guard at the PlayScene boundary.
- **Scope creep** — runtime curve editing (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL) and mixed generated/scripted campaigns (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD) are explicitly out of scope; extra opportunities are recorded as linked work items rather than absorbed here.
- **Assumption (toggle location)** — the opt-in toggle lives in the `GameRules`/settings store rather than the CSV; revisit only if the producer prefers an all-CSV toggle.

## Out of scope

- Player-state adaptation (adjusting the curve from player performance).
- Runtime curve editing UI (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL).
- Replacing boss / asteroid spawning logic.
- Per-level generated-vs-scripted mixing (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD).

## Related work

- **Implement runtime auto-sequencer for dynamic difficulty adjustment (AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X)** — delivered the sequencer this item wires in (`discovered-from`).
- **Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD)** — follow-on enabled by the opt-in toggle (sibling).
- **Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL)** — sibling designer tool; previews curves but does not affect the game.
- **Design a mechanism for calculating how hard an enemy is to survive (AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K)** — delivered the `enemyDifficulty`/`levelDifficulty` scorer and campaign calibration that seed the default curve.
- **Config store / CSV pipeline (AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA)** — the persistence pattern the new curve CSV follows.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §2.4/§2.5 fire rules, §3.2 level themes.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — enemy archetypes/formations.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (Round 1): Does the generated sequence replace `LEVELS` outright, or sit behind a toggle?**
  - Answer (operator): **(b) opt-in, default off** — shipped behaviour stays unchanged until a designer enables it. Additionally the operator asked for a follow-on work item allowing a campaign to **mix generated and scripted levels**.
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Follow-up: created **Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD)**.

- **Q (Round 1): Per-level curves or one whole-run curve?**
  - Answer (operator): **(b) per-level curves with configurable per-level wave counts.**
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Research: the sequencer takes a single `defaultShootEnabled` for a whole call and returns one group per curve entry — a whole-run curve cannot vary the fire rule by level. Read `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`.

- **Q (Round 1): Where does the curve (and its override) live?**
  - Answer (operator): **(b) extend the CSV `configStore` with a new difficulty-curve file.**
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Research: `configStore`/`csv.ts` are CSV-backed and read-only in production; `rules.ts` is the localStorage tunables store. Read `src/core/configStore.ts`, `src/core/csv.ts`.

- **Q (Round 2): When generated mode is enabled, does the campaign skeleton stay fixed?**
  - Answer (operator): **(a) config also defines level count and names — fully data-driven campaign.**
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Note: boss still triggers after the final configured level via existing `WaveManager` behaviour.

- **Q (Round 2): How editable is the new difficulty-curve CSV?**
  - Answer (operator): **as recommended** — route it through the existing CSV pipeline (editable in dev, bundled read-only in production).
  - Source: interactive reply.

- **Q (Round 2): Where do the default target values come from?**
  - Answer (operator): **as recommended** — seed per-level defaults from the current `LEVELS` measured scores, spread non-decreasingly across waves.
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Research: `levelDifficulty(LEVELS[i].waves).score` in `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`; campaign calibration regression in `src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTCP1CKB00480BD** – Diver jumps on return from dive (completed)
- **AH-0MT7V5UH90023XWR** – Clarify enemy health / one-hit destruction model in GDD (completed)
- **AH-0MU0F1T2H003B4K0** – Swarm are too powerful when shooting (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, accepts, actual, adjusting, allow (+182 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: accepts, affect, asteroid, auto, back (+161 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mudiwetp003xc3x, actual, archetypes, asserts, asteroid (+155 more)

# Goal

Verify the audit-runner fixes satisfy all parent acceptance criteria, add regression coverage, and confirm the full project test suite passes.

# Background

The parent work item (AH-0MUDYHPPC008F7PV) has 5 acceptance criteria. AC1 (fingerprint scoping) appears already implemented in `_compute_content_fingerprint` — this task must verify it, and close any remaining gap. AC2-AC3 are implemented by the sibling task. AC4 (no regression on interactive runs) and AC5 (full test suite passes) are verified here.

# Verification tasks

## 1. Verify AC1 — fingerprint scoping

Confirm `_compute_content_fingerprint` no longer includes the global git HEAD sha as a sole invalidation trigger. The existing tests in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` (`TestContentFreshnessGate`) should prove:
- `test_fingerprint_does_not_query_bare_head` — the whole-repo HEAD sha is not a fingerprint input
- `test_fingerprint_stable_for_unrelated_commit` — an unrelated commit leaves the fingerprint unchanged

If any gap remains (e.g. a bare `git rev-parse HEAD` call still leaks in), fix it.

## 2. Verify AC2/AC3 — in-main-slot partial handling and diagnostics

Add/verify tests that:
- A parent audit with children whose ACs are `partial` due to unserviced in-main-slot work reports "Ready to close: Yes" (when parent ACs are met)
- The audit JSON output includes the `children_assessment` diagnostic distinguishing unserviced-in-main-slot children from genuine-not-ready children
- A genuine `partial`/`unmet` child verdict still blocks the parent (regression guard)

## 3. Verify AC4 — no regression on interactive runs

Add/verify tests that:
- In-main-slot mode (`child_in_main_slot=True`) with a serviced child (verdicts parsed as `met`) still honours the full in-main-slot workflow
- Separate-process mode (`child_in_main_slot=False`) is unchanged
- Existing `test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` tests continue to pass

## 4. Verify AC5 — full project test suite

Run the complete project test suite (`/skill:test`) and confirm zero failures. Triage any failures into critical `test-failure` work items per the triage policy.

# Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: `_compute_content_fingerprint` is confirmed (by test) to exclude the global HEAD sha as a sole invalidation trigger
- AC4: Interactive/separate-process audit behaviour is unchanged (regression tests pass)
- AC5: Full project test suite passes with zero failures
- New tests exist that prove AC2 and AC3 behaviour (unserviced in-main-slot partials do not block; diagnostic distinguishes them)

# Key Files
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` — fingerprint tests
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` — in-main-slot tests

## Summary
During AH-0MUH5GKAX00323IJ (Refactor CombatScene to extend CombatCoreScene), a full-suite run reported a single intermittent failure in `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`:

```
FAIL  src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — playable run (AH-0MU7305Z2003NII3) > AC5 — clearing a wave starts a transition, then spawns the next wave
AssertionError: expected false to be true // Object.is equality
 ❯ src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:443:37
    441|     killAllEnemies(scene);
    442|     // Wave 1 wiped → a transition is running (no new enemies yet).
    443|     expect(scene.isTransitioning()).toBe(true);
```

A forced fresh run (`run_tests.py --scope full --force --rerun-failures`) passed, confirming the failure is flaky/timing-sensitive and unrelated to the combat-core refactor. The git state at failure was 4a84c34 (the CombatScene refactor working tree).

## Expected
The wave-transition assertion should be deterministic — clearing the final wave must synchronously (or within a bounded, awaited step) set `isTransitioning()` true before the assertion.

## Investigation hints
- Likely a timing/ordering dependency in the PlayScene wave-transition update loop under parallel test load.
- Consider making the test await the transition-start transition explicitly, or making `killAllEnemies` drive the transition deterministically.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root cause identified (flakiness source).
- [ ] Test (or the underlying transition trigger) made deterministic; the suite passes repeatedly (`--rerun-failures`).
- [ ] No loss of coverage for the wave-transition behaviour.

# Test: shared mineral kill-drop rule

Test-first task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC3, AC5).

## Goal

Write deterministic unit + guard tests that pin the contract of the shared mineral kill-drop rule **before** it is implemented, so `PlayScene` and the gyms provably share one rule.

## Required coverage

- Small asteroid (`getSizeTier() === 'small'`) → exactly one mineral drop at the asteroid's death position.
- Large and medium asteroid → no direct drop (their small split children drop).
- Non-asteroid enemy that absorbed N minerals → re-drops between `mineralRedropFractionMin` and `mineralRedropFractionMax` of N, never more than N, at the death site, using a seeded RNG for determinism.
- Non-asteroid enemy with 0 absorbed minerals → no drops.
- Re-drop scatter stays within `MINERAL_REDROP_SCATTER_RADIUS` of the death site.

## Assumption

Shared helper module path: `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` exporting `resolveMineralKillDrops(scene, entity, rng): Mineral[]` (operator selected the shared-helper approach — see the parent item's Appendix).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid drop + non-asteroid re-drop) has one production definition that both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` consume, and a repo-wide guard asserts it.
- **AC5 — Tests are added and green.** New tests cover the shared rule and the guard; `npm test` for the new files passes.
- The unit tests are deterministic (seeded RNG, no reliance on `Math.random`) and cover every bullet under Required coverage.
- Tests fail before the implementation task lands and pass once it does.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.test.ts` — new.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend guard.
- `src/test/duplicateBodyGuard.ts` — shared guard helper (extend if needed).
- `src/entities/__tests__/BaseEnemy.minerals.test.ts` — keep green / extend.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts` — keep green / extend.

# Wire gyms to the shared mineral kill-drop helper

Implementation task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC1, AC2, AC3).

## Goal

Make every formation gym (including `GymMinerals` and the `GymEnemies` asteroid row) drop minerals on enemy destruction exactly as the game does, by calling the shared helper.

## Minimal implementation

- In `GymFormationScene`, add an injectable RNG (`protected rng: () => number = Math.random` plus a `setRng()`/config seam) used for mineral drops.
- Add a single `_spawnMineralKillDrops(entity)` path that calls `resolveMineralKillDrops(...)` and registers the returned minerals in the gym's mineral field.
- Call it from both the generic destruction path (`onEnemyDestroyed`) and the EXPLODE button (`explodeRandom`), so every destruction path drops exactly once.
- Keep the existing asteroid-split config seam unchanged (splitting stays scene/config-specific).
- Update the `GymMinerals` / `GymFormationScene` docstrings to describe the shared code path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Gyms drop on small-asteroid destruction.** Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` / `GymEnemies` asteroid row spawns exactly one mineral at its position.
- **AC2 — Gyms re-drop for non-asteroid enemies.** In a gym, a non-asteroid enemy re-drops a configured fraction of the absorbed minerals at its death site.
- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid drop + non-asteroid re-drop) has one production definition that both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` consume.
- Large and medium asteroids drop none directly; their small split children do.
- The gym test suites added by the test-first task pass, and `npm test` plus `npm run typecheck` pass.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `onEnemyDestroyed`, `explodeRandom`, RNG seam, mineral field.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts` — docstring/behaviour.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — docstring/behaviour.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` — shared helper (from the previous task).

# Intake brief — Gym↔game behavioural-parity audit

**Headline:** A full evaluation of the scene layer found twelve places where the shipped `PlayScene` and the gym scenes still run **divergent copies of the same behaviour**. This epic tracks extracting each into one shared implementation (or explicitly recording an intentional difference), so that every object behaves identically in every scene and new divergence is caught by an automated guard.

## Problem statement

Operators continue to see errors caused by differences between gym scenes and the game scene. The producer directive is that **gyms and the game must execute the same core code**; the only legitimate difference is that a gym enables a **constrained set of features** (one enemy type, the enemy editor, fixed formations, no campaign/wave progression). Prior epics (`AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO`, `AH-0MUDCT7EU0061OSZ`) unified the eight combat/lifecycle methods onto `CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene`, but the audit below shows that a second tier of behaviour — player control, enemy fire dispatch, projectile lifecycle, power-up drops, minerals, the boss, teleport and the gym base seams — is still duplicated and has already drifted.

## Users

- **As a player**, when I practice in a gym I want every object (player, enemies, asteroids, boss, minerals, power-ups, bullets) to behave exactly as it does in the game, so the gym is a truthful training ground.
- **As a developer**, when I change a behaviour I want to change it in exactly one place, so a scenario cannot drift from the shipped game.
- **As a tester**, I want an automated parity guard that fails when a scene re-introduces a duplicate of a shared method, so regressions are caught before release.
- **As the producer**, I want the "gyms are the parity reference" principle enforced by code structure and tests.

## Evaluation method

Reviewed every production scene under `src/scenes` (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene` and its subclasses `GymEnemies`/`GymBoss`/`GymMinerals`, `GymPlayer`, `GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`) plus the shared cores `CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene`, and the entity/config layer (`enemyFactory`, `BaseEnemy`, `Asteroid`, `Boss`, `Mineral`, `powerups/*`). Compared method inventories, dispatch tables, per-frame sequences and copy-pasted bodies, and cross-checked against the existing worklog so as not to duplicate open items.

## Findings — the gap register

| # | Gap | Evidence (divergent copies) | Impact |
|---|-----|------------------------------|--------|
| 1 | **Player-control step duplicated** | Input→timers→multipliers→physics sequence re-implemented in `PlayScene.tick`, `GymFormationScene.tick`, `GymWeapons.tick`, `GymPowerUpsUtility.tick`, `GymPowerUpsCombat.tick`; `GymPlayer.update` inlines the input-map branch instead of the shared `_readPlayerInput` | Player movement/fire-rate differs between scenes; GymPlayer does not share any control code |
| 2 | **Enemy fire dispatch duplicated** | `PlayScene._fireFor` and `GymEnemies.collectBullets` both hard-code `enemyKey → tryFire*`; `GymPowerUpsCombat._tickScouts` re-implements it again with a **fake fixed 16 ms clock** (`_nextFireTime += 16`) instead of the scene clock | A new enemy type must be wired twice; gym/combat fire cadence is frame-count-based, not time-based |
| 3 | **Projectile lifecycle duplicated** | Enemy-bullet wrap+expiry loop in `PlayScene._advanceBullets`, `GymFormationScene.tick`, `GymPowerUpsCombat._advanceEnemyBullets`; player-bullet advance via `advanceAndCull` in `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene._advancePlayerBullets`, `GymWeapons._advanceBullets`/`advanceBullets` | Wrap/expiry fixes reach one scene only |
| 4 | **Power-up drop layer duplicated & drifted** | Spawner build (`PlayScene._buildDropSpawner` ≈ `GymFormationScene._buildDefaultPowerUpSpawner`); lifecycle+collection (`PlayScene._updateDrops`/`_collectIfOverlapping` ≈ `GymFormationScene._updatePowerUpLayer`/`_collectOverlappingDrops` ≈ `GymWeapons.advanceDrops`/`collectOverlapping` ≈ `GymPowerUpsCombat.advanceDrops`/`_collectOverlapping` ≈ `GymPowerUpsUtility.advanceDrops`/`_collectOverlapping`); **P9 magnet** only in `PlayScene` + `GymPowerUpsUtility`; **P4 bomb notice** only in `PlayScene` + `GymPowerUpsCombat`; **per-type pickup cues** only in `PlayScene`, `GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUpsUtility` | P9/P4/cue behaviour differs between gyms; five copies of the collect loop |
| 5 | **Mineral layer duplicated & drifted** | `PlayScene._handleMinerals` ≈ `GymFormationScene._updateMinerals`; `openMineralChoice`/`selectMineralChoice` duplicated with different contracts (`GameState` + overflow + `MineralChoiceScene{origin,options,strategy}` vs a local `mineralHold` capped and reset to 0 + `MineralChoiceScene{onSelect}`); `MineralChoiceScene` carries both interfaces | Hold overflow, choice wiring and reward application differ between game and gym |
| 6 | **Boss integration diverges** | `PlayScene._updateBoss(dt)` runs inside `tick`; `GymBoss.update` calls `super.tick(dt)` **then** advances the boss, so `GymBoss.tick()` never advances the boss; `PlayScene.getAdditionalTeleportBodies` avoids the boss for P7, `GymBoss` does not; `PlayScene._spawnMinions` (phase minions) has no gym equivalent | Boss behaves differently (bullet timing, teleport safety, minions) in the gym |
| 7 | **Teleport duplicated** | `GymPowerUpsCombat.triggerTeleport` is a full override of the shared `CombatScene.triggerTeleport`, bypassing `canTeleport()` and the hit-radius hooks (hard-codes `ENEMY_HIT_RADIUS`/`BULLET_HIT_RADIUS`) | Teleport safety logic can drift; the gym override is not exercised by shared tests |
| 8 | **Asteroid split duplicated** | Identical `onEntityDestroyed` split closures in `GymEnemies.ts` and `GymMinerals.ts` | A split-physics change must be made twice |
| 9 | **Gym base seams bypassed via casts** | `GymEnemies._onRespawn` reaches into private `entities`/`playerBullets` and re-implements `GymFormationScene._respawnFormation`; `_onTogglePlayer` casts to mutate the base's private `player`/spawn coords | Duplicate respawn logic; fragile casts |
| 10 | **Restart/teardown parity** | `PlayScene._resetRunState` calls `effectsRegistry.reset()`; `GymFormationScene` only recreates the registry when the power-up layer is enabled, and never resets it on teardown, so `GymMinerals`/`GymEnemies` keep permanent effects across a restart | Stale effects after restart in gyms without field drops |
| 11 | **GymPlayer not on the shared control core** | `GymPlayer` extends `Phaser.Scene` and inlines the scheme→input mapping; no shared player tick | The "player" object is the one object with a genuinely separate code path in one gym |
| 12 | **No automated parity guard for the second tier** | The existing `definesMethod` guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) covers only the original eight methods; none of the shared helpers above are guarded, and the cross-scene equivalence test covers only a subset of behaviours | Future divergence is invisible until a user reports a bug |

> **Already tracked (do not duplicate):** mineral **kill-drop** rule — `AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB` (+ children `AH-0MUIGTRFY002JDDS`, `AH-0MUIG1AFG00938TV`, `AH-0MUIGTRVA0072TWW`, `AH-0MUIGTSAX00096Y4`, `AH-0MUIG16QK003MSNO`); "gym-parity principle in AGENTS.md" — `AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1`; beat-clock fire scheduling — `AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B` (+ blocked children). These are referenced as related/blocking rather than re-created.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Each gap in the register has a single shared implementation.** Gaps 1–11 are closed by extracting the duplicated behaviour into the shared core/module or by consuming an existing shared hook; no production scene re-implements a shared behaviour. Verified by the extended duplicate-body guard and by prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **AC2 — Behavioural gaps are closed (or explicitly documented as intentional).** Every behavioural difference identified in gaps 1–11 (P9 magnet in formation gyms, P4 notice, per-type pickup cues, boss-in-`tick`, boss teleport avoidance, teleport gating, hold overflow, restart effect reset, GymPlayer input) is either made identical to the game or recorded as an intentional, approved difference in the epic description and the relevant child.
- [ ] **AC3 — Cross-scene equivalence for every object.** Automated tests boot both `PlayScene` and each gym and assert identical outcomes for the player, each enemy archetype, asteroids (incl. split), the boss, minerals (collection/hold/choice), power-ups (spawn/lifecycle/collect/magnet/bomb/cues) and projectiles under the same input and `dt`.
- [ ] **AC4 — Regression guard.** The repo-wide duplicate-body guard is extended to cover every newly shared method/helper, and a permanent test fails if any production scene re-introduces a copy.
- [ ] **AC5 — No behaviour regression in the game.** `PlayScene` behaviour and all existing tests remain green; any change to game behaviour is called out explicitly in the epic and approved as canonical.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, the gym docstrings and `README.md` describe the shared behaviour modules, the hooks a gym implements, and the constrained-feature (not divergent-code) nature of gyms.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes.** The complete suite (`/skill:test`, `npm test`) passes with zero failures and no newly-flaky tests.

## Constraints

- **Single source of truth:** extract genuinely shared behaviour; do not trade one duplication for another. A shared module must not force game-only concerns (score, waves, lives) into gyms, nor gym-only concerns (editor, fixed formations) into the game.
- **Minimum churn / surgical:** match existing style; do not delete unrelated dead code (report it instead).
- **Preserve public/test seams** (e.g. `getBullets`, `advanceBullets`, `getDrops`, `getCollectAnimations`, `spawnDrop`, `triggerTeleport`, `getPlayerHitCount`, help/back handles).
- **Generics/type-safety:** the shared core is generic (`<TEnemy, TBullet, TDrop>`); additions must not weaken typing.
- **Determinism:** tests drive `tick(dt)`; shared behaviour must be driven by the supplied `dt` and the scene clock — no frame-count fake clocks.
- **UK English** in all written output and docs.
- **Gating:** implementation proceeds only through `/skill:implement`; this item does not authorise code changes.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26 against HEAD)

- Shared cores exist: `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` (input, auto-fire, drop collection) and `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` (collisions, hits, teleport); `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` extend `CombatScene`; `GymPowerUpsCombat` extends `CombatScene`; `GymWeapons`/`GymPowerUpsUtility` extend `CombatCoreScene`.
- The eight-method duplicate guard and cross-scene equivalence tests live in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`; `src/test/duplicateBodyGuard.ts` hosts `definesMethod`/`collectProductionSourceFiles`.
- `GymEnemies` is the single config-driven enemy gym (one row per enemy config on the index); `GymMinerals` is asteroids-only; `GymBoss` is the dedicated 4-phase boss gym; `GymPlayer` is the bare-bones tuning scene.
- Entity classes (`Player`, `Scout`, `Diver`, `Tank`, `Phaser`, `Swarm`, `Boss`, `Asteroid`, `Mineral`) are already shared; the divergence is entirely at the **scene integration** layer.
- Open related items: `AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB` (mineral kill-drop), `AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1` (document parity principle), `AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B` (beat-clock fire scheduling).

## Desired change

Extract/consume shared behaviour for gaps 1–11 and extend the guard for gap 12, via the dependency-ordered child items below. Do not redesign gym feature gating: a gym may still enable only a subset of features and disable others (e.g. scoring), but the code running for an enabled object must be the same code as the game.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — host shared player tick, projectile lifecycle, and teleport hooks.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — delegate duplicated bodies to the shared helpers.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — consume shared helpers; expose protected seams; reset registry.
- `src/scenes/gym/{GymEnemies,GymBoss,GymMinerals,GymPlayer,GymWeapons,GymPowerUpsCombat,GymPowerUpsUtility}.ts` — consume shared helpers, remove local copies/casts.
- `src/scenes/core/<new shared modules>.ts` — e.g. projectile lifecycle, power-up drop layer, mineral layer, enemy fire dispatch.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` / `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — shared enemy-fire seam.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `src/test/duplicateBodyGuard.ts` — extend guard/equivalence.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `README.md` — docs.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — over-abstraction.** Pushing gym-only features into the shared core couples the game to dev tooling. Mitigation: share behaviour only, keep features behind hooks/flags.
- **Risk — behaviour-change ambiguity.** Some divergences may be intentional. Mitigation: each is listed as an OPEN QUESTION below; the default assumption is "the game's behaviour is canonical" unless the producer says otherwise.
- **Risk — test churn.** Both scene suites reach into private internals. Mitigation: keep method names/visibility on the shared base; assert hooks/shared path rather than a class.
- **Risk — scope creep** into a full engine extraction (wave/level system, editor UI). Explicitly out of scope; record extra opportunities as linked items.
- **Assumption:** the shipped game is the canonical behaviour wherever a difference is found, except where an intentional divergence is already approved (e.g. `GymPowerUpsCombat` 0.8 s invulnerability).
- **Assumption:** gyms remain feature-constrained (no campaign/wave progression, optional scoring); "no difference" means no difference in the code path for enabled features, not "the gym must run the campaign".

## Related work

- `AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO` — Unify PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat logic into a shared core (completed, epic).
- `AH-0MUDCT7EU0061OSZ` — Extract shared combat core into standalone gym scenes (completed).
- `AH-0MUHM66ES0027QQV` — Enemy gym P3/P6 hit-gating not shared (completed) — prior example of this class of defect.
- `AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4` — Ability items not functioning (completed) — prior gym/game divergence in choice rewards.
- `AH-0MUD9R4BA004WQEM` — Cross-scene equivalence tests and duplicate-body verification (completed).
- `AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M` — Restore gym-game parity RCA (completed).
- `AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB` — Gym asteroids do not drop minerals (open) — the mineral kill-drop slice of gap 5.
- `AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1` — Document gym-parity principle in AGENTS.md (open) — supports AC6/governance.
- `AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B` — Bullets should fall on the beat (open) — touches gap 2's fire clock.
- `AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL` — Dev Utilities gym scene (open) — future consumer of the shared modules.

## Open questions (canonical-behaviour doubts)

1. **P9 Magnet in formation gyms** — the game and `GymPowerUpsUtility` pull drops toward the ship; `GymFormationScene` (enemy/minerals/boss) does not. Adopt the game behaviour everywhere? *Recommended: yes.*
2. **P4 bomb notice** — game and `GymPowerUpsCombat` show "BOMB! Bullets cleared"; formation gyms do not. Adopt everywhere? *Recommended: yes.*
3. **Per-type pickup cues** — game/weapon/utility gyms play per-type activation cues; formation gyms play only the generic chime. Adopt the game's cue set? *Recommended: yes.*
4. **Boss minions** — the game spawns phase minions (`planMinionSpawns`); `GymBoss` does not. Should the boss gym mirror minion spawning, or is that a deliberately constrained feature? *Recommended: mirror it (behaviour), possibly behind a toggle.*
5. **`GymPowerUpsCombat` invulnerability** — 0.8 s (local hook) vs the game's 1.5 s. Keep the approved exception or converge? *Recommended: keep the hook but document it explicitly as an intentional, approved difference.*
6. **Gym field-drop cadence** — the game drops on a kill chance; gyms drop on a timer. These are different spawn *sources*; is sharing only the lifecycle/collection correct? *Recommended: yes — keep distinct sources, share lifecycle/collection/magnet/notice/cues.*
7. **Mineral hold overflow** — the game carries overflow (`collected − capacity`); the formation gym resets the hold to 0. Adopt overflow? *Recommended: yes.*
8. **GymPlayer scope** — should the bare-bones player gym consume the shared player-control tick/input, or stay deliberately minimal? *Recommended: consume the shared input/physics helper; it need not add enemies.*
9. **Scoring in gyms** — gyms show `SCORE: n/a`. Confirm scoring remains a deliberately disabled feature (not a divergence to fix). *Recommended: yes, keep disabled.*
10. **Enemy-fire seam shape** — shared factory-level dispatcher vs a common `fire(now)` method on `BaseEnemy`. *Recommended: factory-level dispatcher (less invasive to the entity hierarchy).*

## Plan — child work items (dependency-ordered)

| # | Child item | Type | Priority | Depends on | Register gaps |
|---|-----------|------|----------|------------|---------------|
| 1 | Shared player-control step across all scenes | task | critical | — | 1, 11 |
| 2 | Shared enemy-fire dispatch using the real scene clock | task | critical | — | 2 |
| 3 | Shared projectile-lifecycle helper | task | critical | — | 3 |
| 4 | Shared power-up drop layer (spawner, lifecycle, collection, magnet, P4 notice, cues) | task | critical | 3 | 4 |
| 5 | Shared mineral layer (collection, hold/overflow, choice overlay) | task | critical | — | 5 (kill-drop tracked by `AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB`) |
| 6 | Boss integration on the shared tick (+ teleport avoidance, minions) | task | critical | 1 | 6 |
| 7 | Unify teleport: remove `GymPowerUpsCombat` override | task | critical | 3 | 7 |
| 8 | Shared asteroid-split helper and protected gym base seams | task | critical | — | 8, 9 |
| 9 | Restart/teardown parity across gyms | task | critical | — | 10 |
| 10 | Extend parity regression guard and cross-scene equivalence tests | task | critical | 1–9 | 12 |

The dependency graph is acyclic; items 1–3 are foundational, 4 depends on 3, 6 on 1, 7 on 3, and 10 verifies all others.

|---|--------------------|
| 1 | `AH-0MUII39KX007YUQ0` |

## Appendix — clarifying questions & answers

- The operator's seed instruction was explicit: "If in doubt about which is the correct behaviour leave this as an open question in the work item created." Accordingly, no blocking interview was held; the ten behavioural doubts are recorded above as numbered **Open questions** and repeated in the relevant child items.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Are these gaps already tracked?" — Research: `wl search` across mineral/fire/drop/boss/teleport/player terms. Result: the mineral **kill-drop** rule is tracked by `AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB` (+5 children); the parity-principle doc by `AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1`; beat-clock fire scheduling by `AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B`. All other register gaps are untracked; this epic references rather than duplicates the tracked ones.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "What is the code-level evidence for each gap?" — Research: method-inventory extraction across all production scene files, `grep` of `_applyMagnet`/`_playPickupCue`/`onPowerUpCollected`/`EffectsRegistry.reset`/boss `update` call sites, and side-by-side reading of `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymEnemies`, `GymBoss`, `GymMinerals`, `GymPlayer`, `GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`. Evidence is recorded in the Findings table.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

## Problem

Running the test-skill runner (`.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) from inside a linked agent worktree (the mandated implement workflow: `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`) fails with a `live_repo_mutation` error whenever another agent creates a worktree during the (multi-minute) test run — even though the suite itself passes (`failures: []`).

## Root cause

`snapshot_repo_state()` resolves the checkout via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, which from a linked worktree returns the **worktree root**, not the shared repo root. `_parse_worktrees()` then computes `agent_root = <worktree-root>/.worklog/worktrees` — a path that does not exist inside a linked worktree — so the real agent worktrees under `<main-checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/` are never added to `excluded_refs`. Any concurrent `git worktree add --track -b <branch>` is therefore reported as a mutation.

Additionally, `diff_snapshots()` applies `excluded_refs` only to the refs surface, not to `config`: the `branch.<name>.remote` / `branch.<name>.merge` keys written by `git worktree add --track` are reported as added config even from the main checkout, so the same false positive also reproduces there under concurrency.

## Steps to reproduce

1. From a linked worktree, run `python3 .pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py --json --force`.
2. While it runs, create a worktree from the main checkout (e.g. `implement.py start` for another item).
3. Observe `live_repo_mutation` listing the concurrently-created `refs/heads/wl-*` ref and its `branch.*` config keys, with `success: false`.

## Impact

- `/skill:test` cannot reliably populate the audit full-suite cache from a worktree in a multi-agent environment.
- Every retry races the same way; under sustained concurrency the guard can never pass from a worktree.
- `implement.py finish` is unaffected (it calls `run_cached`/npm directly, not this runner), and this repo's pre-push hook only runs `wl sync`, so the gate is not currently a hard blocker — but the audit evidence path is degraded.

## Expected behaviour

Compute the agent-worktree exclusion root from the shared git dir (e.g. `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` → main checkout) rather than `--show-toplevel`, and apply `excluded_refs` to the `config` diff as well as the `refs` diff.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Running the runner from a linked worktree while a concurrent worktree is created elsewhere reports `success: true` when the suite passes.
2. Refs and their associated `branch.<name>.*` config keys for worktrees under `<main-checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/` are excluded from the mutation diff.
3. A genuine suite-caused mutation (fixture branch with no registered worktree, config rewrite, moved `dev`) is still detected and fails the run.

# Full-suite verification and AC audit

## Goal

As a **producer**, I need proof that the wired feature introduces no regressions and that every parent acceptance criterion is satisfied before **Wire the runtime auto-sequencer into the game's wave generation (AH-0MUH6LEYY0054E63)** is marked `in_review`.

## Deliverables

- Run the full project test suite (`npm test`) via `/skill:test`, triaging any failures into critical `test-failure` work items.
- Run `/skill:audit` against the parent and record the result.
- Fix any failures/regressions found within this plan's scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Testing/validation — the full project test suite passes with the new changes (`npm test`).
- No regressions — no previously passing test fails after the changes.
- Audit — `/skill:audit` reports the parent ready for review with all acceptance criteria met.

## Out of scope

- Fixing unrelated pre-existing failures; those are triaged into separate `test-failure` work items.

**Key Files:**

- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` — builder acceptance suite.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — scene toggle-path tests.
- `src/core/configStore.test.ts` — config load/fallback tests.
